page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: A state function is a property whose value
depends only on the present state of the
system, not on the path by which that
steps.why: This is the property Hess law rests on: if a quantity depends only on the state, its change between two states is fixed, whatever route the system takes.
common_mistakes: Defining it as a constant — a state function changes when the state changes; it only ignores the path.
steps.memory_tip: Same state, same value — the history of the system does not enter.
steps.margin_note: The contrast word path must appear.

steps.label: Examples and contrast
lines: Examples: internal energy U, enthalpy H,
entropy S, Gibbs energy G, pressure,
Heat q and work w are not state functions:
their values depend on the path taken.

lines.text: State function: fixed by the state, not the path

steps.why: Listing q and w as the exceptions shows the definition is understood — they describe the transfer of energy along a path, not a state of the system.
common_mistakes: Listing heat or work among the state functions — both are path functions.
steps.memory_tip: The big four letters U, H, S, G are state functions; q and w are the two path functions.
steps.margin_note: Naming q and w as path functions is the strong finish.
